newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the U.S. banking system on Thursday via multi-day system repurchase agreements, economists and analysts said.

Starting today, the Fed will enter the open market between 1030 EST/1530 GMT and 1045 EST/1545 GMT, an hour earlier than what had been normal. The Fed late last year announced the earlier intervention time to conform to busier market conditions.

Economists at UBS Securities expected the Fed to add via four-day system repurchase agreements. "With Tuesday's two-day operation rolling off, the Fed will address the still-significant add need with a week-end add," they said in their Daily Economic Digest.

Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds, agreed, predicting an addition through "term system account RPs." At 0910 EST/1410 GMT, the overnight bank lending or federal funds rate was trading at 5-11/16 percent, above the Fed's 5-1/4-percent target for the rate. On Tuesday, fed funds closed at 5.00 percent.
